items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: I remember George Brunies was in that band... Ted Lewis was there... I used to hear them over the radio... that was one of the experiences that I had with Ted Lewis.

ctx.x: An awful lot has been made about jazz rhyhtms and the beat in jazz, etc. There's always a discussion of the rhythm (Pause) Okay, did you...did those rhythms, how similar to the tribal songs and the tribal dance rhythms did you find jazz rhythms to be? Did you find any similarity or did you find a great deal of difference? Or did you have any difficulty making the adjustment or was it something that you just loved and gravitated toward?

When I said at the beginning of this tape that I think everybody---every human being from days a long time ago---always had some kind of a rhythm and blues....(Pause) And when I think of the years that I spent in Chicago it was really the start of my induction into jazz music, besides the other facets of classical concert work that I did. The background was there and the way that I learned to project listening to all those other bands---at one time when I was in a theater on the North Side of Chicago, Ted Lewis…
